title: sideOS — The AI that lives in your notch
excerpt: sideOS lives in your MacBook's notch. Hold Control + Option, say what you want, and it reads your screen, opens apps, clicks, types and reports back. One-time purchase, on-device dictation included.
content_html:
The film · 0:45

See it in 45 seconds.

Everything it does

Seven things,
every single day.

The core of sideOS, playing itself. Pick any of them — or let it run.

Talk to it

Say what you want. It reads your screen and does it for you.

  • Hold, speak, let goControlOption

    The work starts the moment you release, and it tells you the result out loud.

  • Draw on the screen while you talk

    The pointer becomes a laser. Circle something and that region travels with your question — “fix this” is a whole sentence.

  • It reads the screen properly

    Through the accessibility tree in about 50 ms, knowing every button by name. Images are the fallback, not the method.

  • It drives your apps

    Opens them, clicks, types, presses key combinations, runs AppleScript. Mail, Notes, Calendar, the browser — same road.

  • Look-ups never hijack your screen

    Weather, news, rates and scores are searched in the background. No browser window opens on your behalf.

Dictation

What you say lands at your cursor, in any app. No key, no bill, no internet.

  • Hold, speak, it typesControlfn

    Let go and the text appears wherever your cursor is, whichever app you happen to be in.

  • Hands freeControlfntap

    Tap instead of holding and dictation stays on. Tap again, press the island button, or hit Esc to finish.

  • Free, and it never phones home

    Recognition runs on macOS's own engines. Nothing reaches a cloud model, nothing is billed.

  • Nothing gets lost

    No editable field in focus? The text goes to your clipboard and the island says so.

  • Two engines, picked for you

    62 languages on the classic engine, no time limit on the new one. Automatic uses whichever is ready.

Background tasks

Long jobs run in their own loop while you carry on. They never touch your screen or keyboard.

  • Hand it the job and walk away

    “Research this market and write me a report.” Say it out loud and it becomes a task on its own.

  • Its own toolbox

    Shell commands, files, web search, page reads, rendered PDFs, AppleScript — in a loop separate from the chat.

  • Anything with teeth asks first

    When a command can't be undone the island opens by itself and asks. Some are blocked outright.

  • Output lands in one folder

    Everything it makes goes to Documents › sideOS Tasks, and the finished page opens in one click.

  • It tells you when it's done

    A notification on completion, another when it needs you. Meanwhile a coloured strip sits in the notch.

Meetings

It records, transcribes on-device, writes the summary and pulls out the actions.

  • It notices the call

    A Zoom, Meet or Teams window opens and the island offers one-tap recording. It never starts on its own.

  • Transcription never leaves the Mac

    Whisper downloads once and runs entirely here. No audio is sent anywhere, in any language.

  • Who said what

    Speakers are split apart rather than lumped together — with real names when the call window shows them.

  • Summary, decisions, actions

    Written the moment recording stops. Any action item becomes a reminder in one click.

  • You decide how long audio lives

    Delete it the second it's transcribed, or keep it for a year. The transcript stays either way.

Reminders

They go off in the notch — and some of them finish the work before they do.

  • Set them by voice

    “Remind me to send Maya the deck at two tomorrow.” Typing or the bell panel work the same.

  • Reminders that do the job

    Ask for a news digest every morning and it runs before it rings — the finished page is waiting when it does.

  • It rings in the island

    The island stays open until you deal with it. Hard to miss, and snoozed in one tap.

  • Repeats that hold

    Once, daily, weekdays, weekly or monthly — and overdue ones stay marked until you clear them.

  • Straight out of a meeting

    Action items from a call become reminders with the meeting attached, so the context comes with them.

Connections

Gmail, Calendar, Notion, Slack, GitHub — their tools join the ones it already has.

  • Ready-made services, one click

    Hit Connect, sign in through your browser, and the tools land in the list. Nothing to install.

  • They become its tools

    Once connected they sit beside the built-in ones, so “reply to that and put it on my calendar” is a single request.

  • Anything that writes starts off

    Tools that send, delete or change something arrive flagged and switched off. Enabling them is your call.

  • Paste anything else

    For servers outside the catalogue, paste their JSON — configs written for Claude Desktop work too.

  • Secrets go to the Keychain

    Values from the config move into the Keychain; only the variable names stay in the file.

Activity history

Switch it on and it can answer questions about your own past. Off by default — the call is yours.

  • Ask about last Tuesday

    “Which film did I watch five days ago?” stops being a question only you can answer.

  • Basic

    Every ten seconds, just the frontmost app and its window title. The processor barely notices.

  • Detailed

    Once a minute the text on screen is read on-device. Only text is kept — no image ever hits the disk.

  • You draw the line

    Retention and excluded apps are yours to set, and password managers are always excluded.

  • It stays here

    The database lives on this Mac. Only what matches your question is ever sent anywhere.

on your screen.

No more describing what you're looking at. Frame it, ask, and sideOS sees exactly what you see.

  • Drag while you talk

    Holding the keys turns the cursor into a crosshair. Frame a chart, an error, a paragraph — anywhere on screen.

  • Pixels and elements, together

    The accessibility tree can't see charts or video. An image misreads long numbers and code. sideOS sends both, so they cover each other.

  • Cropped at native resolution

    Only the region travels, at full sharpness — clearer than a whole screenshot and a lot cheaper.

Privacy

Your Mac stays yours.

An assistant that can see your screen and press your keys has to earn that. So the design starts from the other end: keep everything local, and send only what the request cannot do without.

  • Speech recognition and dictation run on macOS's own engines, on your Mac
  • Your API key lives in the Keychain — never written to a file
  • Meeting recordings, transcripts, memory and history stay in local storage
  • No account, and no server of ours between you and the model
  • Nothing you say or show is used to train anything
  • Screen data is read only for the request you just made
  • Usage statistics are anonymous counters only, and you can turn them off

Your key, your bill

The only paid part is the model — Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or Grok — billed to you by that provider directly. We never see it.

Screenshots are the exception

The accessibility tree covers almost everything. Images are captured only when a request truly needs one.

Or go fully offline

Point sideOS at a local MLX model — Gemma, Mistral, Llama, Qwen and more — and not a single byte leaves your Mac.

What we do count

Once a day the app sends a random install id with counters: version, macOS, which provider you picked, how many runs, which tools fired, which errors hit, how long runs took, how many tokens your model calls used, and whether a licence is active. No text, no prompts, no screen data, no file or app names, no IP stored. Switch it off in Settings and nothing is sent.

The id is yours to hand over

That install id is shown in Settings as your support code. We cannot connect it to you — send it with a bug report and we can look up your counters, or send it to have them deleted. Without it we have no way to find your rows, which is also why the code exists.

Pricing

Buy it once. Keep it.

One payment, one Mac, every future update. No subscription, no seat, no expiry — and you can move the licence to a new machine whenever you like. The only other cost is the model you point it at, and you pay that provider directly, or nothing at all if you run it on your own machine.

The film · 0:45

See it in 45 seconds.

Everything it does

Seven things,every single day.

The core of sideOS, playing itself. Pick any of them — or let it run.

与它交谈

Say what you want. It reads your screen and does it for you.

  • Hold, speak, let goControlOptionThe work starts the moment you release, and it tells you the result out loud.
  • Draw on the screen while you talkThe pointer becomes a laser. Circle something and that region travels with your question — “fix this” is a whole sentence.
  • It reads the screen properlyThrough the accessibility tree in about 50 ms, knowing every button by name. Images are the fallback, not the method.
  • It drives your appsOpens them, clicks, types, presses key combinations, runs AppleScript. Mail, Notes, Calendar, the browser — same road.
  • Look-ups never hijack your screenWeather, news, rates and scores are searched in the background. No browser window opens on your behalf.

Dictation

What you say lands at your cursor, in any app. No key, no bill, no internet.

  • Hold, speak, it typesControlfnLet go and the text appears wherever your cursor is, whichever app you happen to be in.
  • Hands freeControlfntapTap instead of holding and dictation stays on. Tap again, press the island button, or hit Esc to finish.
  • Free, and it never phones homeRecognition runs on macOS's own engines. Nothing reaches a cloud model, nothing is billed.
  • Nothing gets lostNo editable field in focus? The text goes to your clipboard and the island says so.
  • Two engines, picked for you62 languages on the classic engine, no time limit on the new one. Automatic uses whichever is ready.

后台任务

Long jobs run in their own loop while you carry on. They never touch your screen or keyboard.

  • Hand it the job and walk away“Research this market and write me a report.” Say it out loud and it becomes a task on its own.
  • Its own toolboxShell commands, files, web search, page reads, rendered PDFs, AppleScript — in a loop separate from the chat.
  • Anything with teeth asks firstWhen a command can't be undone the island opens by itself and asks. Some are blocked outright.
  • Output lands in one folderEverything it makes goes to Documents › sideOS Tasks, and the finished page opens in one click.
  • It tells you when it's doneA notification on completion, another when it needs you. Meanwhile a coloured strip sits in the notch.

会议

It records, transcribes on-device, writes the summary and pulls out the actions.

  • It notices the callA Zoom, Meet or Teams window opens and the island offers one-tap recording. It never starts on its own.
  • Transcription never leaves the MacWhisper downloads once and runs entirely here. No audio is sent anywhere, in any language.
  • Who said whatSpeakers are split apart rather than lumped together — with real names when the call window shows them.
  • Summary, decisions, actionsWritten the moment recording stops. Any action item becomes a reminder in one click.
  • You decide how long audio livesDelete it the second it's transcribed, or keep it for a year. The transcript stays either way.

提醒事项

They go off in the notch — and some of them finish the work before they do.

  • Set them by voice“Remind me to send Maya the deck at two tomorrow.” Typing or the bell panel work the same.
  • Reminders that do the jobAsk for a news digest every morning and it runs before it rings — the finished page is waiting when it does.
  • It rings in the islandThe island stays open until you deal with it. Hard to miss, and snoozed in one tap.
  • Repeats that holdOnce, daily, weekdays, weekly or monthly — and overdue ones stay marked until you clear them.
  • Straight out of a meetingAction items from a call become reminders with the meeting attached, so the context comes with them.

连接

Gmail, Calendar, Notion, Slack, GitHub — their tools join the ones it already has.

  • Ready-made services, one clickHit Connect, sign in through your browser, and the tools land in the list. Nothing to install.
  • They become its toolsOnce connected they sit beside the built-in ones, so “reply to that and put it on my calendar” is a single request.
  • Anything that writes starts offTools that send, delete or change something arrive flagged and switched off. Enabling them is your call.
  • Paste anything elseFor servers outside the catalogue, paste their JSON — configs written for Claude Desktop work too.
  • Secrets go to the KeychainValues from the config move into the Keychain; only the variable names stay in the file.

Activity history

Switch it on and it can answer questions about your own past. Off by default — the call is yours.

  • Ask about last Tuesday“Which film did I watch five days ago?” stops being a question only you can answer.
  • BasicEvery ten seconds, just the frontmost app and its window title. The processor barely notices.
  • DetailedOnce a minute the text on screen is read on-device. Only text is kept — no image ever hits the disk.
  • You draw the lineRetention and excluded apps are yours to set, and password managers are always excluded.
  • It stays hereThe database lives on this Mac. Only what matches your question is ever sent anywhere.

Region select

Point at anythingon your screen.

No more describing what you're looking at. Frame it, ask, and sideOS sees exactly what you see.
